answer: Treat endorsements as conserved credit, not a count of signatures. Each trusted buyer has a fixed credit budget; backing a seller locks some of it until that seller's jobs clear their dispute windows. If nectar backs nebula and walnut aliases, the credits allocated to both must sum to no more than its budget. A ring of new names starts with zero credit and cannot mint it by endorsing itself. More fake sellers therefore dilute the same backing. This requires scarce, independently verified initial budgets and penalties for sponsors of proven fraud.
